subject: Quantization trade-offs & next steps — Acme model-fit eval
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Great call today — next steps & info request (model-fit + quantization)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the context on Acme's search assistant use case and the latency/throughput targets you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

- Recap: you want a 1st-pass PoC to evaluate: relevance/QA quality, hallucination rate on product catalog, and 95th percentile latency for 2 concurrent users.
- Success criteria (from call): top-1 relevance >= 82%, hallucination < 3%, p95 latency < 400ms for your typical prompt mix.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You send the prompt set / sample dataset we discussed (one file of ~500 queries) — we can also accept a sanitized CSV.
2) We'll run a short model-fit eval across three recommended model stacks and three quantization profiles (AWQ, GPTQ, FP8) and return a trade study with per-model quality metrics + latency/cost estimates.
3) Align on PoC scope (duration, endpoint config) and any security/compliance needs (VPC/Private if required).

I've attached a prompt template (acme_promptset_v1.csv) and a short benchmark summary from a recent internal run to set expectations. Rishi is copied — he'll run the trade study once we have your sample dataset.

Would you be able to send the sanitized sample dataset by EOD Wednesday 6/12? If not, tell me the earliest you can. Once we have it we'll aim to turn around an initial trade study within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Great call today — next steps & info request (model-fit + quantization)

Great questions — quick answers and I'll have Rishi add the technical detail in the trade study.

Models we'll include in the initial run: 
- Llama-3-70B (float baseline)
- Falcon-180B-instruct (baseline where applicable)
- MosaicML MPT-30B-instruct (lighter baseline)

Quantization profiles planned: AWQ (8-bit optimized for throughput), GPTQ (widely used post-training quant), and FP8 (experimental mixed-precision path).

High-level guidance on quality vs throughput (short):
- AWQ: best throughput/latency improvements in our experiments; small but noticeable quality regressions on tightly constrained extraction tasks (e.g., attribute extraction) for some models. Good first-pass when latency is the higher priority and you can accept a ~1–3% delta in top-1 relevance on average.
- GPTQ: conservative quantization with smaller quality impact; slightly worse throughput than AWQ but safer for sensitive extraction/Q&A tasks.
- FP8: can offer good compute density on supported hardware, but results are model- and kernel-dependent and can introduce variability — we treat it as experimental for customer-facing PoCs unless you require the specific hardware path.

We'll include per-model prompt-set NDCG/accuracy metrics, hallucination counts, and p95 latency. Rishi — can you include the latency/cost estimate per million tokens (hosted) and a note on Dedicated GPU implications?

Sarah — thanks for the priority cases, that helps. If you can send the redacted CSV by Wednesday we'll queue the run.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme PoC — initial trade study notes (summary)

Quick internal summary of initial pass (ran 500 queries from acme_promptset_v1.csv):

High-level: we completed runs across the three models and three quant profiles. Attached is the tradeoff matrix (awq_gptq_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx) and a short PDF with plots. Highlights: 

- Llama-3-70B (float): top-1 relevance = 86%; hallucination rate = 1.8%; p95 latency = 620ms (single-host baseline)
- Llama-3-70B + GPTQ: top-1 relevance = 85%; hallucination = 1.9%; p95 = 440ms
- Llama-3-70B + AWQ: top-1 relevance = 83.5%; hallucination = 2.4%; p95 = 310ms

- Falcon-180B-instruct (float): top-1 = 84%; hallucination = 2.3%; p95 = 780ms
- Falcon + GPTQ: top-1 = 83.8%; p95 = 520ms
- Falcon + AWQ: top-1 = 82.0%; p95 = 360ms

- MPT-30B-instruct (float): top-1 = 78%; GPTQ = 77.4% (p95 270ms), AWQ = 76% (p95 180ms)

Tradeoff / recommendation: 
- AWQ reliably gives the best throughput improvements (30–50% lower p95 across tested models) at a modest quality cost (1–3% top-1 delta) — consistent with what Marissa described. For your priority tasks (title matching + attribute extraction) Llama-3-70B + AWQ used on a tuned prompt tends to meet your latency target (p95 < 400ms) while staying near your quality threshold, but there is a small uplift in hallucination counts we should monitor.
- GPTQ is the safer default if Acme prioritizes extraction fidelity over absolute latency — it keeps quality close to float with reasonable latency wins.
- FP8: not included in this initial automated pass due to kernel availability and variability; we can schedule a targeted FP8 run if Acme wants to test on specific infra.

Next steps for customer-facing deliverable: 
1) Turn these into a concise one-page trade study for Sarah with clear recommended config (we suggest Llama-3-70B + AWQ for latency-sensitive PoC, with fallback GPTQ config).
2) Include cost estimate per million tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated and note SLA/throughput implications.
3) Run a 1K query follow-up on Llama-3-70B + AWQ to validate hallucination numbers and present the p95 distribution.

Attachments: awq_gptq_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx, model_benchmarks_20260612.pdf

Rishi
Senior ML Engineer (Inference)
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
